newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel hopes Khatami will turn Iran toward peace.
newsitem.headline: Israel hopes Khatami will turn Iran toward peace.

text.p: Israel on Monday said the installation of Iran's new president, Mohammed Khatami, gave Tehran a chance to "open a new page" in relations with its neighbours and prove it was "leaning toward peace".
An Israeli Foreign Ministry statement said the Jewish state had the right to demand "good neighbourly conduct" from Iran and would judge Khatami's government on its deeds.

Khatami, a 54-year-old Shi'ite Moslem cleric known for his moderate views, formally took office on Monday vowing to work for a lawful society and open dialogue with any nation that respected the Islamic republic.

"Iran is given an opportunity to open a new page in her relations with all of her neighbours and to prove that she is leaning toward peace and not toward confrontation," the Israeli Foreign Ministry statement said.
Khatami defeated conservative Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri in a landslide election victory in May promising to introduce social reforms and to increase personal freedom.

Tehran condemns the Middle East peace process between Israel and its Arab neighbors as a sellout of Palestinian rights. Khatami opposes the peace process, but has said he will not take action to disrupt it.

"It is the right of the ancient Iranian people to choose the regime it desires. However, it is the right and the duty of the countries neighbouring Iran and of the entire international community to demand...norms of accepted international behaviour and good neighbourly conduct," the Israeli statement said.
"Israel will follow with keen interest the behaviour of the new government in Iran and will judge it according to its words and deeds," it said.

Israel accuses Tehran of developing nuclear and other non-conventional weapons to point at the Jewish state, and of arming Hizbollah (Party of God) militants who battle Israeli troops in south Lebanon.
Israel also says Iran is responsible for the fate of missing airman Ron Arad, whose bomber was shot down over Lebanon in 1986. Tehran denies any knowledge of his whereabouts.
